titleEn: Behind the Ears, Tie It Tight!

pages.text: "Grandma, tie this for me!" Mumu brought a headband cord onto the porch. Grandma always tied it. Preparing the meal, she waved. "Shall you try today?"
"By myself? Then I'll do it!" Mumu gripped the cord. "I'm bounding around today, so it needs to be tight." Mumu placed it on their head.
But it kept catching on their ears. Pulling made it slide over their eyes. "Oh, it won't work!" Everything went dark.
After finally removing it, Mumu bowed their head, eyes full of tears. "I can't even tie a cord..."
Quick-handed monkey Taro jumped onto the porch. "It keeps catching on your ears." He gently laid one ear down to show Mumu.
"Let your ears lie down and pass the cord behind them." Taro traced a path behind an ear. "Behind the Ears, Tie It Tight!"
Mumu turned their ears, forward and back. "Oh! There's a path behind them!" Mumu slipped the cord behind the ears. This time, it did not catch.
Mumu tied the two ends firmly at the front. Shaking their head or bounding did not move it. "I tied it myself!"
Mumu untied it and started again. "One, lay my ears down gently! Two, cord behind the ears! Three, tie tightly in front!" The next morning, Mumu did not call Grandma.

Grandma hugged Mumu and rubbed foreheads with them. Something that seemed hard became easy for the hands once they found the way. Still in Grandma's arms, Mumu pointed to the knot above their forehead. "Behind the Ears, Tie It Tight!"
